- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment is negative but model ignores it).  
- Underestimate sharp upward moves when sentiment is negative but recent prices are rising.  
- Overshoot downward corrections after strong upward moves — model lags in recognizing momentum reversal.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect after strong trends, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast slope; avoid aggressive upward revisions.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices — adjust downward by 1–2% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is weak.  
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model tends to overreact — cap upward revisions at 1.5x recent peak unless sentiment turns positive.
